<h1>Eden M. Melles</h1>

<h2>PhD Candidate in Political Science</h2>

<p class="institution">Northwestern University</p>

<p>
I am a PhD candidate in the Department of Political Science at Northwestern University. 
My research examines heterogeneity within group politics primarily with respect to migration and identity. 
My dissertation project, Borders Beyond Borders: Migration, Identity, and the Transnational Political Behavior of 
the Eritrean Diaspora, investigates the political and identity socialization processes that Black immigrants undergo in their 
home countries and in the United States. I conduct an in-depth case study of Eritrean immigrants in the United States
to illustrate the profound impact salient historical events in the home country, migration pathways, and transnational politics have on
shaping the process of identity formation and political behavior. Ultimately, my project illuminates novel theoretical and empirical insights
that helps bridge literature in Race and Ethnicity, American, and Comparative politics, by emphasizing the importance of geopolitical 
relationships in the formation of identity and political behaviors. 

My work has been supported through the National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship, American Political Science Association,
and the Northwestern University Graduate School. My research has been published in the Journal of Race, Ethnicity, and Politics as well as 
PS: Political Science & Politics.

## Research

My research focuses on heterogeneity within group politics, with broader interests in
race and ethnicity, migration, and political behavior.

My current research projects investigate:

- **Borders Beyond Borders: Migration, Identity, and the Transnational Political Behavior of 
the Eritrean Diaspora** — How the process of identity formation and political socialization is shaped through transnational processes.
- **Black and Ethnic: Theorizing New Approaches to the Study of Black Immigrants in
the United States** — Investigates how aggregation bias in the study of Black immigrants can obscure meaningful within group heterogeneity.
- **Investigating the Naturalization Gap: Determinants of
Immigrant Political Participation in the US** — Explores how time to naturalization in the US has impacts on immigrant political participation.
